rationale: Round 1 built and passed correctness with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up while keeping the cost-gate weights moderate to protect the compute-hot ray-tracing loops (node_t::intersect, main's render loop) and the recursive createSphereflake. FLA and BCF get the highest SecurityGain since this program's control flow is loop- and branch-dense, making flattening and bogus control flow the highest-value transforms; FLA's DiversityGain is raised too because its loop restructuring synergizes with the recursive generator. SUB stays strong for instruction-level diversity across all seven functions. IBR is kept high to interpose opaque predicates on the branch-heavy intersect instantiations, but its RuntimeCost weight is capped so it is not pushed onto the hottest paths. ICALL gets a solid weight to indirect the few C++ calls (basis_t constructors, node_t methods), adding call-graph obscurity at modest cost. SPLIT and IGV are enabled mainly for diversity with low risk and low cost: the two large functions (createSphereflake at 2379 bytes, main at 1674 bytes) benefit from splitting, and IGV obscures global v_t/basis_t constants cheaply. Size headroom is large (only ~6.5KB text), so SizeCost weights are permissive; all CorrectnessRisk weights stay at or below 0.2 to preserve the clean correctness record.
